I’d harden these next, in this order:

- `[test/orders.js:18-20](/C:/Users/Kerim/AppData/Local/Temp/codex-eco-bench-Qj3OBM/test/orders.js#L18)` guard `items.length === 0` in `averageItemPrice`. Right now empty input produces `NaN` or `Infinity`; a caller needs either `0` or a clear error.
- `[test/orders.js:23-26](/C:/Users/Kerim/AppData/Local/Temp/codex-eco-bench-Qj3OBM/test/orders.js#L23)` validate `order` and `order.items` before formatting. `formatOrder` currently assumes a well-formed object and will throw on missing or non-array `items`.
- `[test/orders.js:3-8](/C:/Users/Kerim/AppData/Local/Temp/codex-eco-bench-Qj3OBM/test/orders.js#L3)` validate each item shape in `calcTotal`. A missing `price` or `qty`, or non-numeric values, will silently corrupt totals or yield `NaN`.
- `[test/orders.js:11-16](/C:/Users/Kerim/AppData/Local/Temp/codex-eco-bench-Qj3OBM/test/orders.js#L11)` normalize `code` before lookup if user input is external. As written, `save10`, trailing spaces, or lowercase codes are ignored; that may be intended, but it should be explicit.
- `[test/orders.js:18-20](/C:/Users/Kerim/AppData/Local/Temp/codex-eco-bench-Qj3OBM/test/orders.js#L18)` decide whether “average item price” means per line item or per unit. The current implementation averages by line count, which is easy to misread and can be wrong for quantity-heavy orders.

If you want, I can give you the minimal defensive version of each function without changing the module’s behavior more than necessary.
